newsitem.title: USA: Seagull optimistic about deep gas well.
newsitem.headline: Seagull optimistic about deep gas well.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp chairman Barry Galt said on Tuesday the company had seen enough in still-incomplete tests on an 18,000-feet deep natural gas well in south Texas to be optimistic about its prospects.

Galt said at the company's shareholders meeting that a first test well into the extremely deep "Lower Wilcox" formation near Wharton, Texas, was not completed because of mechanical problems, but a second well was now being drilled.
Results from the first attempt were sufficient to give Seagull "continuing optimism," Galt said.

"We were disappointed by the mechanical problems, but what we did see in the deeper penetrations of the (first) well served only to heighten our enthusiasm for the potential that our position in this Lower Wilcox play represents," he said.

Galt said he expected the second test well to be completed by the end of this quarter, but would not comment further. "The second well, which is headed back to the Big Mamou (large gas reserve) that we think may be there, is still simply not far enough along," he told Reuters after the meeting.

Galt would not comment on consensus estimates that Seagull will earn $0.48 a share this year, but said prices for oil and gas were "quite satisfactory. "We foresee healthy demand and reasonably firm prices (for natural gas) for the rest of 1997," he said.
